So, in order to find the argument of \({@aa@}{@sigb@}{@bbi@}\), we consider the argument of \({@abs(aa) + abs(bb/i)@}\cdot i\), where \(a = {@abs(aa)@}\) and \(b = {@abs(bb/i)@}\) and then use the symmetry of the unit circle to find the value of \(\theta\) within the correct range.

In the case of \({@abs(aa) + abs(bb/i)@}\cdot i\), \(\theta = \tan^{-1}\left( \frac{{@abs(bb/i)@}}{{@abs(aa)@}}\right) \)

\(= \tan^{-1}\left( {@abs(bb/i)/abs(aa)@}\right) \)
